event.text: Implement the spec, task by task.
I'll start by reading the spec and tasks files.

1	---
2	feature: Repo map
3	status: approved
4	---
5	
6	# Repo map
7	
8	## Goal
9	A reconcile or implement session starts knowing what the workspace is made of, so it spends its turns on the work instead of on discovering the shape of the repo. A mechanical build walks the workspace and records what it finds: the projects and their paths, the folder conventions the tree actually follows, and, per project, an index of its public types and members. The small part — projects and conventions — is given to the session up front; the type index stays on disk and is read when a session needs a signature, so a large repo costs tool calls it would have spent anyway rather than context it cannot afford. Blind planning never sees any of it.
10	
11	## Building the map
12	Run on demand from the command, and by the session start that needs a fresh map.
13	
14	- B1 (docs/features/repo-map.md#Repo map): the command `KiwiAgent: Build Repo Map` writes the map: the workspace's projects — solutions, `.csproj`, `package.json` workspaces — each with its path and kind, and for each project a type index of its public types with their public members, one line each.
15	  - E1: a workspace where no project is recognised still produces a map that states it found none, so the next session start does not rebuild over and over.
16	- B2: the build considers the workspace's source and project files only, skipping the locations the agent's own search tools skip, the agent's generated folder, and — when the workspace has a `.gitignore` — what it ignores; the same set is what "the newest source file" is measured over.
17	  - E7: a workspace with no `.gitignore`, or one that cannot be read, builds normally on the built-in list of skipped locations alone.
18	- B3 (docs/features/repo-map.md#Repo map): the type index of a project comes from the build's own scan of its source for `public` declarations, C# and TypeScript alike; no language service is consulted.
19	  - E2: a file the scan cannot parse is left out of the index and named as skipped there, and does not fail the build.
20	- B4 (docs/features/repo-map.md#Repo map): folder conventions are stated as facts derived from the tree alone, never from any document, and each carries the evidence it rests on ("endpoints live in `src/<Feature>/Endpoint.cs` — 14 of 15").
21	  - E3: a pattern with too few occurrences, or with counterexamples beyond the threshold, is left out entirely rather than stated with a hedge.
22	- B5: the build runs without an engine: no model call, no tokens, no permission prompt.
23	- B6: the build is deterministic — run twice over an unchanged tree it produces byte-identical files, with ordering that does not depend on filesystem enumeration order.
24	- B7: the build replaces its files wholesale and atomically, and two builds asked for at once (two session starts, or the command during a start) resolve to a single build; no reader ever sees a partly written file.
25	
26	## Starting a session that needs the map
27	A reconcile run or an implement session begins, and the map has to be there and current before the first prompt.
28	
29	- B8 (docs/features/repo-map.md#Repo map): a reconcile run and an implement session receive the map's summary as context at their start; a chat session and a plan session do not.
30	  - E4 (docs/intent/agent.md#Phase 1: Blind plan): the map's root is in no plan session's read scope, so its Read and Glob deny it and blindness holds even when a map exists.
31	- B9 (docs/features/repo-map.md#Repo map): when the map is missing or older than the newest source file, the start builds it first and the session's first prompt is held until the build ends; progress is visible while it runs.
32	  - E5: a build that fails, or exceeds its time bound, does not block the start — the session begins with the previous map if there is one and with none if there is not, and says which.
33	  - E6: a session works from the map as it stood when it started and keeps that snapshot for its life — another session's build, or the command, rewriting the map underneath changes nothing it holds; a session set up afresh after its engine stopped counts as a start and takes a new snapshot.
34	- B10: the injected summary is size-bounded — the project list, the folder conventions, and per project the path to its type index and the number of public types in it. Where the bound trimmed the list, the summary states how many projects were left out.
35	
36	## Reading a project's types
37	A session that needs an actual signature goes to the index instead of the source.
38	
39	- B11: each project's type index is a file on disk whose path the injected summary names, readable with the session's ordinary read and search tools; it is not size-capped, because it is read on demand and searched, not injected.
40	- B12 (docs/intent/agent.md#Retrieval): the retrieval sub-session reads the same index files with its own tools; nothing about the map is injected into it.
41	- B13: the map's files are generated output: a write into them is not refused, it is lost — the next build rewrites them wholesale, so nothing a session edits there survives.
42	
43	## Findings
44	| Finding | Proposed solution |
45	|---|---|
46	| F1 (naive, B11): a reconcile run cannot read anything under `.agent/`. `ScopeGuard.check` (src/agent/phases/scope-guard.ts) matches the workspace-relative path against the scope's globs, and `reconcileScope` (src/agent/phases/reconcile.ts) gives `readable: ['**']`; `**` does not match a path whose segment starts with a dot, so Read and Grep of `.agent/...` are denied with "this phase is limited to **". The spec should say the index files are reachable only where the phase's scope names their root, so the map's root is added to the reconcile scope (the task, once ruled). | Put plainly: B11 assumes that having read tools is the same as being allowed to read the file, and it is not — each phase is given a list of paths its tools may open, and the map's folder is not on the reconcile run's list, so every read of it is refused. The map's content does not change; only the spec's claim about reachability, which should say the map lives where each phase that needs it is permitted to read, and that permission is part of building this feature. |
47	| F2 (naive, E6): a session's context is not fixed at its start. `SessionManager.ensureLive` (src/agent/session/session-manager.ts) recreates the engine on the next prompt whenever it stopped — window reload, close, a turn that ended the engine — and `setupFor`/`modeSetup` (src/extension.ts) rebuild the system prompt then, so a resumed reconcile or implement session would be given the map as it stands at that moment and would run the staleness check again. The spec should say what a resumed session gets. [resolved] | Agreed, E6 claims more than intended: it only rules out the map changing under a session mid-flight. Revise E6 to say a running session's map never changes beneath it, and a session set up afresh after its engine stopped is a start — it checks staleness and takes the map as it then stands. |
48	| F3 (naive, B3): no language service is reachable from the code as it stands. Nothing under src/agent imports `vscode` (only src/extension.ts and src/chat/*), and `typescript` is a devDependency of a bundled extension (`vsce package --no-dependencies`). The only in-process route is `vscode.executeDocumentSymbolProvider` from the extension layer, which yields an empty result both when no provider is registered and while one is still loading, so "available" cannot be asked. The spec should say an empty or failed answer counts as unavailable and the project falls back, and the user rules whether the TypeScript index is worth bundling `typescript`; the task for the language-service route waits on that ruling. [resolved] | Agreed on availability: revise E2 so a language service counts as available only when it answers, an empty or failed answer being no answer, and that project falls back. On the ruling I propose the scan is the whole of B3 for now and the language-service route is dropped from this feature — it buys fidelity this map does not need and costs a bundled dependency plus a `vscode` reach from the agent layer. |
49	| F4 (naive, B2): nothing in the code reads what the workspace ignores. The only shared notion of skipped locations is `IGNORED_DIRS` in src/agent/openai-session/tools/glob.ts (node_modules, .git, bin, obj, dist, out, .vs, .idea), used by glob.ts and grep.ts; no `.gitignore` is parsed anywhere, and `.agent` is not in the set. The spec should say the build skips the same locations the agent's search tools skip, plus `.agent/`, or accept a gitignore reader as new work with no library for it. [resolved] | Agreed, and I propose the first reading: revise B2 to say the build skips what the agent's own search tools skip, plus the agent's generated folder, and drop "what the workspace ignores". A gitignore reader is a separate concern that would change search as much as the map, and one shared notion of where we do not look is worth more than precision here. |
50	| F5 (naive, B13): nothing stops a session writing into the map. `modeSetup` (src/extension.ts) gives implement and chat sessions no `ScopeGuard`, and the Allow-writes switch (src/agent/permissions/write-allowance.ts) lets a write through without a prompt; docs/intent/agent.md#Phase 3: Implement says implement has "no scope guard". B13 as written is a property of the build, not a rule the code holds. The spec should say so, or a deny rule on the map's path becomes the task. [resolved] | B13 should stand, reworded rather than enforced: revise it to say an edit into the map is lost at the next build, not refused. A deny rule would be the one scope guard on a phase intent deliberately leaves unguarded, for a file whose content is disposable anyway. |
51	| F6 (contradiction, E4): `blindPlanScope` (src/agent/phases/blind-plan.ts) lets a plan session read `docs/**`, the root README and its own three plan files — not `docs/intent/**` as E4 says, citing docs/intent/agent.md#Phase 1: Blind plan ("Tools: Read/Glob scoped to `docs/intent/**`"), while the same document's Intent write-back section says "Phase 1 is blind: it reads `docs/**` and nothing else". The map stays out of reach on either wording; a test written to E4's wording fails. [resolved] | Agreed, E4 borrowed a scope definition it has no business restating. Revise E4 to state only what this feature owns — the map's root is in no plan-phase read scope, so a plan session cannot reach it — and drop the `docs/intent/**` wording; which docs blind planning reads is that feature's question, not this one's. |
52	| F7 (naive, B12): there is no retrieval sub-session. Nothing in src implements `retrieve` or any sub-session other than the reconcile and cleanup child runs (src/chat/chat-view-provider.ts `startMapping`, `startCleanup`), and docs/features/README.md still lists retrieval-subsession.md as left to build. B12 cannot be delivered or proven by this feature; the spec should either drop it or state it as a constraint on the retrieval feature when that is built. | Agreed: mark B12 removed. Nothing in this feature can deliver or prove it, and the rule it carries — the sub-session reads the index files, nothing injected — belongs to the retrieval feature, so I would record it as an intent amendment on that feature's doc instead. |
53	| F8 (naive, B11): the index files would sit where search cannot reach them. The map's home is `.agent/` — the only generated root the code has (`RunLog.forSession` in src/agent/runs/run-log.ts, `SKILL_ROOTS` in src/agent/skills/skill-index.ts) — and this workspace's `.gitignore` ignores `.agent/`. On the default profile (`kiwiAgent.profiles` in package.json, engine `claude-sdk`) a session's Read/Glob/Grep are Claude Code's own, since `SdkSession` (src/agent/sdk-session/sdk-session.ts) passes tool names only, and those pass over what the workspace ignores; the extension's own `globTool` (src/agent/openai-session/tools/glob.ts) hands the pattern to node's `glob`, which does not match a dot-prefixed segment either. Read by an exact path works; searching the index, which B11 rests on, does not. The spec should say a session opens an index by the path the summary names, or the map should live outside the ignored root. | Agreed, and I propose keeping the map in the generated root and revising B11 to say a session opens an index by the path the summary names, dropping "searched" — generated, disposable output does not belong in the tracked tree just to be greppable, and the summary already hands over every path. What that costs is the "which project holds type X" sweep across indexes; the project list and conventions usually answer it, and if they prove not to, a lookup is its own feature rather than a reason to move the files. |
54

1	import { readFile, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
2	import { join } from 'node:path'
3	import { PLAN_DIR, featureSlug } from './blind-plan'
4	import { bodyOf, frontMatterValue, withFrontMatterValue } from './spec-file'
5	
6	/**
7	 * The feature's task board, `plan/<slug>.tasks.md`: what to build and where,
8	 * written by the mapping run once the spec is settled, and marked by the
9	 * implementer as it goes. The file is the only state: markers survive a fresh
10	 * session and the plan view reads them as they are.
11	 */
12	
13	/** `blocked` is unfinished work with a reason; only `tested` is a finish. */
14	export type TaskState = 'open' | 'in_progress' | 'done' | 'tested' | 'blocked'
15	
16	/** The test that proves one delivered item: the evidence shown on the spec. */
17	export type Proof = { item: string; file: string; test: string }
18	
19	export type Task = {
20	  id: string
21	  /** The line's text after the id, markers included, as written. */
22	  text: string
23	  /** Spec item ids the task delivers (B1, E2). */
24	  delivers: string[]
25	  /** Workspace-relative paths the task touches; what verification runs over. */
26	  files: string[]
27	  /** Paths the mapping run read to reach the task: what the implementer starts from and does not have to find again. */
28	  context: string[]
29	  /** What the implementer proved, item by item. */
30	  proves: Proof[]
31	  state: TaskState
32	  /** The mapping run says the task is gone. */
33	  removed: boolean
34	}
35	
36	/** One run of the test commands, newest first in the file. */
37	export type VerificationRecord = { at: string; ok: boolean; text: string }
38	
39	export type TasksState =
40	  | { exists: false }
41	  | {
42	      exists: true
43	      tasks: Task[]
44	      verification: VerificationRecord | undefined
45	      /** Fingerprint of the spec the board was mapped from; absent on a board written before the stamp existed. */
46	      spec: string | undefined
47	    }
48	
49	export const VERIFICATION_SECTION = 'Verification'
50	const SPEC_KEY = 'spec'
51	
52	export function tasksPath(cwd: string, feature: string): string {
53	  return join(cwd, PLAN_DIR, `${featureSlug(feature)}.tasks.md`)
54	}
55	
56	/** Workspace-relative path of the tasks file, the form used in prompts and scopes. */
57	export function tasksFile(feature: string): string {
58	  return `${PLAN_DIR}/${featureSlug(feature)}.tasks.md`
59	}
60	
61	const TASK = /^-\s+(T\d+)\b\s*(?:\(([^)]*)\))?\s*:\s*(.*)$/
62	const FILES = /^\s+-\s+files\s*:\s*(.*)$/i
63	const CONTEXT = /^\s+-\s+context\s*:\s*(.*)$/i
64	const PROVES = /^\s+-\s+proves\s*:\s*(.*)$/i
65	const PROOF = /^([A-Z]{1,3}\d+)\s+(\S+)\s+(.+)$/
66	const HEADING = /^#{1,6}\s+(.*)$/
67	const RECORD = /^-\s+(\S+)\s*:\s*(passed|failed)\b\s*,?\s*(.*)$/i
68	const REMOVED = /\[removed\]/i
69	const BLOCKED = /\[blocked\b/i
70	const TESTED = /\[tested\]/i
71	const DONE = /\[done\]/i
72	const IN_PROGRESS = /\[in progress\]/i
73	
74	/** Blocked wins over any finish: a task marked tested and then blocked on a re-run is not finished. */
75	function stateOf(text: string): TaskState {
76	  if (BLOCKED.test(text)) return 'blocked'
77	  if (TESTED.test(text)) return 'tested'
78	  if (DONE.test(text)) return 'done'
79	  if (IN_PROGRESS.test(text)) return 'in_progress'
80	  return 'open'
81	}
82	
83	const list = (text: string): string[] =>
84	  text
85	    .split(',')
86	    .map((s) => s.trim())
87	    .filter((s) => s.length > 0)
88	
89	/** `src/a.ts (new)` names a file the task creates; the path is what matters downstream. */
90	const pathOf = (entry: string): string => entry.replace(/\s*\(new\)\s*$/i, '').trim()
91	
92	/** `B1 test/a.test.ts a_rule_holds`; an entry that does not parse is kept out, not guessed at. */
93	function proofs(text: string): Proof[] {
94	  return list(text).flatMap((entry) => {
95	    const match = PROOF.exec(entry)
96	    return match ? [{ item: match[1]!, file: match[2]!, test: match[3]!.trim() }] : []
97	  })
98	}
99	
100	export function parseTasks(text: string): { tasks: Task[]; verification: VerificationRecord | undefined; spec: string | undefined } {
101	  const tasks: Task[] = []
102	  let task: Task | undefined
103	  let inVerification = false
104	  let verification: VerificationRecord | undefined
105	  for (const raw of bodyOf(text).split(/\r?\n/)) {
106	    const line = raw.trimEnd()
107	    const heading = HEADING.exec(line.trim())
108	    if (heading) {
109	      inVerification = heading[1]!.trim() === VERIFICATION_SECTION
110	      task = undefined
111	      continue
112	    }
113	    if (inVerification) {
114	      const record = RECORD.exec(line.trim())
115	      // Newest first: the first record under the heading is the one that counts.
116	      if (record && !verification) {
117	        verification = { at: record[1]!, ok: record[2]!.toLowerCase() === 'passed', text: record[3]!.trim() }
118	      }
119	      continue
120	    }
121	    const files = FILES.exec(line)
122	    if (files && task) {
123	      task.files = list(files[1]!).map(pathOf)
124	      continue
125	    }
126	    const context = CONTEXT.exec(line)
127	    if (context && task) {
128	      task.context = list(context[1]!)
129	      continue
130	    }
131	    const proves = PROVES.exec(line)
132	    if (proves && task) {
133	      task.proves = proofs(proves[1]!)
134	      continue
135	    }
136	    const match = TASK.exec(line.trim())
137	    if (!match) continue
138	    const body = match[3]!.trim()
139	    task = {
140	      id: match[1]!,
141	      text: body,
142	      delivers: list(match[2] ?? ''),
143	      files: [],
144	      context: [],
145	      proves: [],
146	      state: stateOf(body),
147	      removed: REMOVED.test(body),
148	    }
149	    tasks.push(task)
150	  }
151	  return { tasks, verification, spec: frontMatterValue(text, SPEC_KEY) }
152	}
153	
154	export async function readTasks(path: string): Promise<TasksState> {
155	  try {
156	    return { exists: true, ...parseTasks(await readFile(path, 'utf8')) }
157	  } catch (error) {
158	    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'ENOENT') return { exists: false }
159	    throw error
160	  }
161	}
162	
163	export const liveTasks = (tasks: Task[]): Task[] => tasks.filter((t) => !t.removed)
164	
165	/** Work has started: some task carries a marker. */
166	export const started = (tasks: Task[]): boolean => liveTasks(tasks).some((t) => t.state !== 'open')
167	
168	/**
169	 * Nothing is left to build. Derived from the markers rather than held anywhere
170	 * else, so it cannot go stale: a task added later makes the feature unfinished
171	 * again by itself.
172	 */
173	export function tasksDone(tasks: Task[]): boolean {
174	  const live = liveTasks(tasks)
175	  return live.length > 0 && live.every((t) => t.state === 'tested')
176	}
177	
178	/** Every file the live tasks name, once each, in file order. */
179	export function taskFiles(tasks: Task[]): string[] {
180	  return [...new Set(liveTasks(tasks).flatMap((t) => t.files))]
181	}
182	
183	/** The live task that delivers an item, first in file order. */
184	export function deliveredBy(tasks: Task[], item: string): Task | undefined {
185	  return liveTasks(tasks).find((t) => t.delivers.includes(item))
186	}
187	
188	/** The proof a live task recorded for an item. */
189	export function provenBy(tasks: Task[], item: string): Proof | undefined {
190	  return liveTasks(tasks).flatMap((t) => t.proves).find((p) => p.item === item)
191	}
192	
193	/** Items a task marked tested without naming a test for: a finish the evidence does not back. */
194	export function unprovenItems(tasks: Task[]): string[] {
195	  return liveTasks(tasks)
196	    .filter((t) => t.state === 'tested')
197	    .flatMap((t) => t.delivers.filter((item) => !t.proves.some((p) => p.item === item)))
198	}
199	
200	/** Of the given item ids, those no live task delivers. */
201	export function undeliveredItems(tasks: Task[], items: string[]): string[] {
202	  return items.filter((item) => deliveredBy(tasks, item) === undefined)
203	}
204	
205	/** The board was mapped from the spec as it stands now. A board without a stamp is taken as fresh: it predates the stamp. */
206	export function tasksFresh(tasks: Extract<TasksState, { exists: true }>, fingerprint: string): boolean {
207	  return tasks.spec === undefined || tasks.spec === fingerprint
208	}
209	
210	export const withSpecFingerprint = (text: string, fingerprint: string): string => withFrontMatterValue(text, SPEC_KEY, fingerprint)
211	
212	export async function stampSpecFingerprint(path: string, fingerprint: string): Promise<void> {
213	  const text = await readFile(path, 'utf8')
214	  await writeFile(path, withSpecFingerprint(text, fingerprint), 'utf8')
215	}
216	
217	export function renderRecord(record: VerificationRecord): string {
218	  return `- ${record.at}: ${record.ok ? 'passed' : 'failed'}${record.text ? `, ${record.text}` : ''}`
219	}
220

1	# Repo map
2	
3	A generated overview of the workspace that reconcile and implement sessions get up front, so they explore less.
4	
5	- Command `KiwiAgent: Build Repo Map` writes `.agent/repo-map.md`; it also runs before a reconcile or implement session starts when the file is older than the newest source file.
6	- Contents: the project list (solutions, `.csproj`, `package.json` workspaces) with paths; per project the public types and their members, one line each; the folder conventions found (test projects, where endpoints, domain models and migrations live).
7	- For .NET the type index comes from the C# language service when available, otherwise from a Roslyn-free scan of `public` declarations; for TypeScript from the TypeScript language service.
8	- Size-bounded: a per-project cap on listed types, and a total cap, with counts of what was omitted, so the map stays a map.
9	- The map is injected as context at session start, not read through tools, and is also readable by the retrieval sub-session.
10	- Folder conventions are stated as facts ("endpoints live in `src/<Feature>/Endpoint.cs`"), derived from the tree, never from the docs.
11	
12	Not included: call graphs, cross-project dependency analysis, watching for changes during a session.

5	/** Code lines a unit of each kind may have; 0 turns the limit off. */
6	export type Thresholds = { functionLines: number; typeLines: number; fileLines: number }
7	
8	export type Oversized = Unit & { path: string; threshold: number }
9	
10	/** Beyond this a file is not measured: it is generated or data, not a unit anyone splits. */
11	const MAX_BYTES = 1_000_000
12	
13	const limitFor = (kind: UnitKind, thresholds: Thresholds): number =>
14	  kind === 'function' ? thresholds.functionLines : kind === 'type' ? thresholds.typeLines : thresholds.fileLines
15	
16	export const anyLimit = (thresholds: Thresholds): boolean =>
17	  thresholds.functionLines > 0 || thresholds.typeLines > 0 || thresholds.fileLines > 0
18	
19	/** The units strictly over their kind's limit; a limit of 0 flags nothing. */
20	export function oversized(path: string, units: Unit[], thresholds: Thresholds): Oversized[] {
21	  return units.flatMap((unit) => {
22	    const threshold = limitFor(unit.kind, thresholds)
23	    return threshold > 0 && unit.lines > threshold ? [{ ...unit, path, threshold }] : []
24	  })
25	}
26	
27	/**
28	 * The oversized units across files, in the order given. A file that is gone,
29	 * binary, too large or matched by an ignore glob is passed over: nothing to
30	 * split there, or nothing anyone wants split (tests, generated code).
31	 */
32	export async function oversizedFiles(cwd: string, files: string[], thresholds: Thresholds, ignore: string[]): Promise<Oversized[]> {
33	  const found: Oversized[] = []
34	  for (const path of files) {
35	    const rel = relative(cwd, path).split('\\').join('/')
36	    if (ignore.some((glob) => matchesGlob(rel, glob))) continue
37	    const text = await readText(path)
38	    if (text === undefined) continue
39	    found.push(...oversized(path, measureUnits(path, text), thresholds))
40	  }
41	  return found
42	}
43	
44	async function readText(path: string): Promise<string | undefined> {
45	  try {
46	    if ((await stat(path)).size > MAX_BYTES) return undefined
47	    const text = await readFile(path, 'utf8')
48	    return text.includes('\u0000') ? undefined : text
49	  } catch {
50	    // Deleted or moved since it was edited: nothing to measure.
51	    return undefined
52	  }
53	}
54	
55	/** One line per unit, as the cleanup run reads it: `src/a.ts:12 name (function, 61 lines, limit 25)`. */
56	export function sizeReport(cwd: string, items: Oversized[]): string {
57	  return items
58	    .map((u) => `${relative(cwd, u.path).split('\\').join('/')}:${u.line} ${u.name} (${u.kind}, ${u.lines} lines, limit ${u.threshold})`)
59	    .join('\n')
60	}

8	/**
9	 * Brings a feature's plan files to the contract. What can be done by rule is
10	 * done here: a legacy task section becomes the tasks file, ids the planner
11	 * renamed are followed through every file, the board is stamped. What needs
12	 * judgment (scenarios, nesting, folding restated rules) is left to the
13	 * planner, whose prompt the caller sends when `problems` remain; running this
14	 * again after that turn finishes the job.
15	 */
16	
17	export type MigrationReport = {
18	  feature: string
19	  /** What was changed on disk, one line each. */
20	  steps: string[]
21	  /** What still departs from the contract, for the planner. */
22	  problems: string[]
23	}
24	
25	const SECTION = /^##\s+(.*)$/
26	const TASKS_HEADING = 'Tasks'
27	/** Old form: `- T1: text (B1, B2) [done]`; the delivered ids trailed the text. */
28	const TRAILING_IDS = /^-\s+(T\d+)\s*:\s*(.*?)\s*\(([A-Z]{1,3}\d+(?:\s*,\s*[A-Z]{1,3}\d+)*)\)\s*((?:\[[^\]]*\]\s*)*)$/
29	/** `- B7: text (was I3)`: the planner's note that a folded item survived under a new id. */
30	const WAS = /^(\s*-\s+([A-Z]{1,3}\d+)\b.*?)\s*\(was\s+([A-Z]{1,3}\d+)\)\s*$/
31	
32	/** Lifts a `## Tasks` section out of the spec as tasks-file lines, ids first. */
33	export function extractLegacyTasks(specText: string): { spec: string; tasks: string[] } {
34	  const lines = specText.split(/\r?\n/)
35	  const kept: string[] = []
36	  const tasks: string[] = []
37	  let inTasks = false
38	  for (const line of lines) {
39	    const heading = SECTION.exec(line.trim())
40	    if (heading) inTasks = heading[1]!.trim().toLowerCase() === TASKS_HEADING.toLowerCase()
41	    if (!inTasks) {
42	      kept.push(line)
43	      continue
44	    }
45	    if (heading || line.trim().length === 0) continue
46	    const trailing = TRAILING_IDS.exec(line.trim())
47	    if (trailing) {
48	      const markers = trailing[4]!.trim()
49	      tasks.push(`- ${trailing[1]} (${trailing[3]}): ${trailing[2]}${markers ? ` ${markers}` : ''}`)
50	    } else tasks.push(line.trimEnd())
51	  }
52	  return { spec: kept.join('\n').replace(/\n{3,}/g, '\n\n'), tasks }
53	}
54	
55	/** Strips the planner's `(was X)` notes and returns what they say: old id → new id. */
56	export function collectRenames(specText: string): { spec: string; renames: Map<string, string> } {
57	  const renames = new Map<string, string>()
58	  const lines = specText.split(/\r?\n/).map((line) => {
59	    const match = WAS.exec(line)
60	    if (!match) return line
61	    renames.set(match[3]!, match[2]!)
62	    return match[1]!
63	  })
64	  return { spec: lines.join('\n'), renames }
65	}
66	
67	/** Rewrites every whole-word occurrence of a renamed id, in whatever file refers to it. */
68	export function applyRenames(text: string, renames: Map<string, string>): string {
69	  let result = text
70	  for (const [from, to] of renames) result = result.replace(new RegExp(`\\b${from}\\b`, 'g'), to)
71	  return result
72	}
73	
74	async function readIfThere(path: string): Promise<string | undefined> {
75	  try {
76	    return await readFile(path, 'utf8')
77	  } catch (error) {
78	    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'ENOENT') return undefined
79	    throw error
80	  }
81	}
82	
83	/** The mechanical part, safe to run any number of times. */
84	export async function migratePlan(cwd: string, feature: string): Promise<MigrationReport> {
85	  const report: MigrationReport = { feature, steps: [], problems: [] }
86	  const spec = specPath(cwd, feature)
87	  const tasks = tasksPath(cwd, feature)
88	  const review = reviewPath(cwd, feature)
89	  let specText = await readIfThere(spec)
90	  if (specText === undefined) {
91	    report.problems.push('no spec file.')
92	    return report
93	  }
94	  const before = specText
95	
96	  const legacy = extractLegacyTasks(specText)
97	  if (legacy.tasks.length > 0) {
98	    specText = legacy.spec
99	    const existing = await readIfThere(tasks)
100	    if (existing === undefined) {
101	      const title = /^#\s+(.*)$/m.exec(specText)?.[1]?.trim() ?? feature
102	      await writeFile(tasks, `# Tasks for ${title}\n\n${legacy.tasks.join('\n')}\n`, 'utf8')
103	      report.steps.push(`moved ${legacy.tasks.length} task line(s) from the spec into the tasks file.`)
104	    } else report.steps.push('dropped the spec’s task section; the tasks file already holds the board.')
105	  }
106	
107	  const renamed = collectRenames(specText)
108	  if (renamed.renames.size > 0) {
109	    specText = applyRenames(renamed.spec, renamed.renames)
110	    const pairs = [...renamed.renames].map(([from, to]) => `${from} → ${to}`).join(', ')
111	    for (const path of [review, tasks]) {
112	      const text = await readIfThere(path)
113	      if (text === undefined) continue
114	      const next = applyRenames(text, renamed.renames)
115	      if (next !== text) await writeFile(path, next, 'utf8')
116	    }
117	    report.steps.push(`renamed ${pairs} across the spec, the review and the tasks file.`)
118	  }
119	
120	  if (specText !== before) await writeFile(spec, specText, 'utf8')
121	
122	  const parsed = parseSpecText(specText)
123	  const board = await readTasks(tasks)
124	  if (board.exists && board.spec === undefined && parsed.problems.length === 0) {
125	    await stampSpecFingerprint(tasks, specFingerprint(parsed))
126	    report.steps.push('stamped the tasks file with the spec it was mapped from.')
127	  }
128	
129	  try {
130	    await readAmendments(intentPath(cwd, feature))
131	  } catch (error) {
132	    report.problems.push(`intent file cannot be read: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`)
133	  }
134	  report.problems.push(...parsed.problems)
135	  return report
136	}

15	 * talk its way around it. A blind planner reads intent docs and writes one
16	 * spec; everything else is denied with the reason. A write inside the scope
17	 * is the phase's deliverable, so it goes through without a permission prompt.

19	export class ScopeGuard implements SessionHooks {
20	  constructor(
21	    private readonly cwd: string,
22	    private readonly scope: Scope,
23	  ) {}

25	  async preToolUse(tool: ToolUse): Promise<PreToolUseOutcome> {
26	    const input = (typeof tool.input === 'object' && tool.input !== null ? tool.input : {}) as Record<string, unknown>
27	    switch (tool.toolName) {
28	      case 'Read':
29	        return this.check(input['file_path'], this.scope.readable, 'read')
30	      case 'Glob':
31	      case 'Grep':
32	        return this.check(input['path'] ?? '.', this.scope.readable, 'search', true)
33	      case 'Write':
34	      case 'Edit':
35	      case 'MultiEdit':
36	        return this.check(input['file_path'], this.scope.writable, 'write') ?? { allow: true }
37	      case 'NotebookEdit':
38	        return this.check(input['notebook_path'], this.scope.writable, 'write') ?? { allow: true }
39	      case 'Bash':
40	      case 'PowerShell':
41	        return { deny: `${tool.toolName} is not available in this phase.` }

44	    }

47	  private check(raw: unknown, globs: string[], verb: string, directory = false): PreToolUseOutcome {
48	    if (typeof raw !== 'string') return { deny: `Cannot ${verb}: no path given.` }
49	    const absolute = isAbsolute(raw) ? raw : resolve(this.cwd, raw)
50	    const rel = relative(this.cwd, absolute).split('\\').join('/')
51	    if (rel.startsWith('..')) return { deny: `Cannot ${verb} outside the workspace: ${raw}` }
52	    const ignored = (this.scope.ignored ?? []).find((g) => matchesGlob(rel, g) || (directory && matchesGlob(`${rel}/x`, g)))
53	    if (ignored) return { deny: `Cannot ${verb} ${raw}: excluded from this phase by the ignore setting (${ignored}).` }
54	    // A search directory must itself lie inside the allowed tree: searching
55	    // from the workspace root would list names of files the phase must not see.
56	    const allowed = globs.some((g) => matchesGlob(rel, g) || (directory && matchesGlob(`${rel}/x`, g)))
57	    if (allowed) return undefined
58	    return { deny: `Cannot ${verb} ${raw}: this phase is limited to ${globs.join(', ')}.` }
59	  }

128	/** What a run under a session is doing right now, as the plan bar shows it; undefined when the event says nothing worth showing. */
129	export function progressLine(event: SessionEvent, label = 'Check'): string | undefined {
130	  switch (event.type) {
131	    case 'tool_call':
132	      return toolLine(event.name, event.input)
133	    case 'assistant_message': {
134	      const first = event.text.split(/\r?\n/).find((l) => l.trim().length > 0)?.trim()
135	      return first ? clip(first) : undefined
136	    }
137	    case 'error':
138	      return `${label} failed: ${clip(event.message)}`
139	    default:
140	      return undefined
141	  }
142	}
143	
144	function toolLine(name: string, raw: unknown): string {
145	  const input = (typeof raw === 'object' && raw !== null ? raw : {}) as Record<string, unknown>
146	  const text = (key: string): string | undefined => (typeof input[key] === 'string' ? (input[key] as string) : undefined)
147	  switch (name) {
148	    case 'Read':
149	    case 'Edit':
150	    case 'Write':
151	      return clip(`${name} ${text('file_path') ?? ''}`)
152	    case 'Grep':
153	      return clip(`Grep "${text('pattern') ?? ''}" in ${text('path') ?? '.'}`)
154	    case 'Glob':
155	      return clip(`Glob ${text('pattern') ?? ''} in ${text('path') ?? '.'}`)
156	    case 'Skill':
157	      return clip(`Skill ${text('name') ?? text('skill') ?? ''}`)
158	    default:
159	      return name
160	  }
161	}
162	
163	function clip(text: string, max = 100): string {
164	  return text.length > max ? `${text.slice(0, max - 1)}…` : text
165	}

1	import { isAbsolute, matchesGlob, relative, resolve } from 'node:path'
2	import type { PreToolUseOutcome, SessionHooks, ToolUse } from '../session/hooks'
3	
4	export type Scope = {
5	  /** Globs, workspace-relative, of what Read and Glob may see. */
6	  readable: string[]
7	  /** Globs, workspace-relative, of what Write and Edit may touch. */
8	  writable: string[]
9	  /** Globs carved out of `readable`; a match is denied even when readable allows it. */
10	  ignored?: string[]
11	}
12	
13	/**
14	 * Enforces a phase's file scope at the tool call, where the model cannot
15	 * talk its way around it. A blind planner reads intent docs and writes one
16	 * spec; everything else is denied with the reason. A write inside the scope
17	 * is the phase's deliverable, so it goes through without a permission prompt.
18	 */
19	export class ScopeGuard implements SessionHooks {
20	  constructor(
21	    private readonly cwd: string,
22	    private readonly scope: Scope,
23	  ) {}
24	
25	  async preToolUse(tool: ToolUse): Promise<PreToolUseOutcome> {
26	    const input = (typeof tool.input === 'object' && tool.input !== null ? tool.input : {}) as Record<string, unknown>
27	    switch (tool.toolName) {
28	      case 'Read':
29	        return this.check(input['file_path'], this.scope.readable, 'read')
30	      case 'Glob':
31	      case 'Grep':
32	        return this.check(input['path'] ?? '.', this.scope.readable, 'search', true)
33	      case 'Write':
34	      case 'Edit':
35	      case 'MultiEdit':
36	        return this.check(input['file_path'], this.scope.writable, 'write') ?? { allow: true }
37	      case 'NotebookEdit':
38	        return this.check(input['notebook_path'], this.scope.writable, 'write') ?? { allow: true }
39	      case 'Bash':
40	      case 'PowerShell':
41	        return { deny: `${tool.toolName} is not available in this phase.` }
42	      default:
43	        return undefined
44	    }
45	  }
46	
47	  private check(raw: unknown, globs: string[], verb: string, directory = false): PreToolUseOutcome {
48	    if (typeof raw !== 'string') return { deny: `Cannot ${verb}: no path given.` }
49	    const absolute = isAbsolute(raw) ? raw : resolve(this.cwd, raw)
50	    const rel = relative(this.cwd, absolute).split('\\').join('/')
51	    if (rel.startsWith('..')) return { deny: `Cannot ${verb} outside the workspace: ${raw}` }
52	    const ignored = (this.scope.ignored ?? []).find((g) => matchesGlob(rel, g) || (directory && matchesGlob(`${rel}/x`, g)))
53	    if (ignored) return { deny: `Cannot ${verb} ${raw}: excluded from this phase by the ignore setting (${ignored}).` }
54	    // A search directory must itself lie inside the allowed tree: searching
55	    // from the workspace root would list names of files the phase must not see.
56	    const allowed = globs.some((g) => matchesGlob(rel, g) || (directory && matchesGlob(`${rel}/x`, g)))
57	    if (allowed) return undefined
58	    return { deny: `Cannot ${verb} ${raw}: this phase is limited to ${globs.join(', ')}.` }
59	  }
60	}

6	# Repo map
7	
8	## Goal
9	A reconcile or implement session starts knowing what the workspace is made of, so it spends its turns on the work instead of on discovering the shape of the repo. A mechanical build walks the workspace and records what it finds: the projects and their paths, the folder conventions the tree actually follows, and, per project, an index of its public types and members. The small part — projects and conventions — is given to the session up front; the type index stays on disk and is read when a session needs a signature, so a large repo costs tool calls it would have spent anyway rather than context it cannot afford. Blind planning never sees any of it.
10	
11	## Building the map
12	Run on demand from the command, and by the session start that needs a fresh map.
13	
14	- B1 (docs/features/repo-map.md#Repo map): the command `KiwiAgent: Build Repo Map` writes the map: the workspace's projects — solutions, `.csproj`, `package.json` workspaces — each with its path and kind, and for each project a type index of its public types with their public members, one line each.
15	  - E1: a workspace where no project is recognised still produces a map that states it found none, so the next session start does not rebuild over and over.
16	- B2: the build considers the workspace's source and project files only, skipping the locations the agent's own search tools skip, the agent's generated folder, and — when the workspace has a `.gitignore` — what it ignores; the same set is what "the newest source file" is measured over.
17	  - E7: a workspace with no `.gitignore`, or one that cannot be read, builds normally on the built-in list of skipped locations alone.
18	- B3 (docs/features/repo-map.md#Repo map): the type index of a project comes from the build's own scan of its source for `public` declarations, C# and TypeScript alike; no language service is consulted.
19	  - E2: a file the scan cannot parse is left out of the index and named as skipped there, and does not fail the build.
20	- B4 (docs/features/repo-map.md#Repo map): folder conventions are stated as facts derived from the tree alone, never from any document, and each carries the evidence it rests on ("endpoints live in `src/<Feature>/Endpoint.cs` — 14 of 15").
21	  - E3: a pattern with too few occurrences, or with counterexamples beyond the threshold, is left out entirely rather than stated with a hedge.
22	- B5: the build runs without an engine: no model call, no tokens, no permission prompt.
23	- B6: the build is deterministic — run twice over an unchanged tree it produces byte-identical files, with ordering that does not depend on filesystem enumeration order.
24	- B7: the build replaces its files wholesale and atomically, and two builds asked for at once (two session starts, or the command during a start) resolve to a single build; no reader ever sees a partly written file.
25	
26	## Starting a session that needs the map
27	A reconcile run or an implement session begins, and the map has to be there and current before the first prompt.
28	
29	- B8 (docs/features/repo-map.md#Repo map): a reconcile run and an implement session receive the map's summary as context at their start; a chat session and a plan session do not.
30	  - E4 (docs/intent/agent.md#Phase 1: Blind plan): the map's root is in no plan session's read scope, so its Read and Glob deny it and blindness holds even when a map exists.
31	- B9 (docs/features/repo-map.md#Repo map): when the map is missing or older than the newest source file, the start builds it first and the session's first prompt is held until the build ends; progress is visible while it runs.
32	  - E5: a build that fails, or exceeds its time bound, does not block the start — the session begins with the previous map if there is one and with none if there is not, and says which.
33	  - E6: a session works from the map as it stood when it started and keeps that snapshot for its life — another session's build, or the command, rewriting the map underneath changes nothing it holds; a session set up afresh after its engine stopped counts as a start and takes a new snapshot.
34	- B10: the injected summary is size-bounded — the project list, the folder conventions, and per project the path to its type index and the number of public types in it. Where the bound trimmed the list, the summary states how many projects were left out.
35	
36	## Reading a project's types
37	A session that needs an actual signature goes to the index instead of the source.
38	
39	- B11: each project's type index is a file on disk whose path the injected summary names, readable with the session's ordinary read and search tools; it is not size-capped, because it is read on demand and searched, not injected.
40	- B12 (docs/intent/agent.md#Retrieval): the retrieval sub-session reads the same index files with its own tools; nothing about the map is injected into it.
41	- B13: the map's files are generated output: a write into them is not refused, it is lost — the next build rewrites them wholesale, so nothing a session edits there survives.
42	
43	## Findings
44	| Finding | Proposed solution |
45	|---|---|

The map is built entirely host-side under `.agent/repo-map/`: a single workspace walk feeds project discovery, a brace-depth scan for `public`/`export` declarations per project, and folder conventions read off the tree, all written through one staging-dir-and-rename replace so builds are deterministic, atomic, shared between concurrent callers, and wholesale — an edit into the map is simply lost.
